_comment: Local model catalog. Review each upstream model card and license before use. Every file comes from the model authors' own repositories or from the quantized conversions named in MODEL_LICENSES.md; weights are downloaded separately, never redistributed by this project. A file with a "convert" step is made on the user's PC from the official files in its "sources" (downloaded into "source_dest"), by the named install step, and published only when its size and SHA-256 equal the entry's; the step runs only while that file is missing, and "delete_sources_after" removes the sources once it is verified (they stay pinned and can be downloaded again). "equivalents" names files of earlier installations that hold the same weights (in the file's folder, or in the one "dest" names), so they count as installed; one with the file's own SHA-256 is the same bytes and is hard-linked into place under the catalog name. size_gb is the installed size.

models.name: Wan 2.2 A14B FP8 — fast image to video
models.description: The Wan 2.2 image-to-video experts with LightX2V's 4-step distillation (the _1022 LoRAs) merged in, in scaled FP8 (e4m3, one scale per output channel): FP8 tensor-core products on RTX 40-series and newer cards (expanded to bf16 elsewhere). The low-noise expert is LightX2V's published file; the high-noise expert is made on this PC from the image-to-video entry's GGUF Q6_K expert and its LoRA in the same layout (LightX2V's published high-noise file holds another distillation). The Full set's image-to-video runs each in place of its GGUF expert and LoRA once a check of the file confirms the merged LoRA. The text encoder, VAE and frame interpolation come from the image-to-video entry.
models.license: Apache 2.0 (LightX2V's distilled Wan 2.2 low-noise weights; the high-noise expert made from QuantStack's GGUF conversion of Wan-AI's Wan 2.2 A14B and LightX2V's 4-step LoRA)

models.name: Wan 2.2 A14B FP8 — fast text to video
models.description: The Wan 2.2 text-to-video experts with LightX2V's 4-step distillation (the _1217 LoRAs) merged in, in scaled FP8 (e4m3, one scale per output channel), like the fast image-to-video experts: FP8 tensor-core products on RTX 40-series and newer cards, without the GGUF experts' Q6_K unpacking and 400 LoRA hooks in every step (about 10 s instead of 15 s per step on the test PC). Both are made on this PC from the Full set's text-to-video GGUF experts and LoRAs, which stay installed: the Full set runs each one in place of its GGUF expert and LoRA once a check of the file confirms the merged LoRA. The text encoder, VAE and frame interpolation come from the text-to-video entry.
models.license: Apache 2.0 (made from QuantStack's GGUF conversion of Wan-AI's Wan 2.2 A14B text to video and LightX2V's 4-step LoRAs)

models.name: InfiniteTalk — talking animated characters
models.description: Lip-synced talking video for animated films: Wan 2.1 image to video (14B, 480p) in LightX2V's 4-step distilled FP8 release with MeiGen-AI's single-speaker InfiniteTalk audio adapter, its CLIP ViT-H image encoder and the chinese-wav2vec2-base speech encoder. Shares the Wan VAE and UMT5 text encoder.
models.license: Apache 2.0 (MeiGen-AI InfiniteTalk adapter, LightX2V's distilled Wan 2.1 I2V 480p, Wan-AI CLIP encoder); MIT (TencentGameMate chinese-wav2vec2-base)

models.name: Index-AniSora V3.2 — motion for anime and 2D cartoon films
models.description: The image-to-video experts of Anime and 2D cartoon films (and of the owner's styles that start from them): the Bilibili Index team's AniSora V3.2, a full fine-tune of both Wan 2.2 A14B image-to-video experts on anime and cartoon footage (motion, line work and timing of animation). Each expert is made on this PC from the official float32 release with LightX2V's 4-step distillation (the _1022 LoRAs) merged in, in scaled FP8 (e4m3, one scale per output channel), the layout of the fast FP8 image-to-video experts; the float32 files (2 x 57 GB) are downloaded for that step and deleted once the result is verified. Only the Full set runs them. The text encoder, VAE and frame interpolation come from the image-to-video entry.
models.license: Apache 2.0 (Bilibili Index team's Index-AniSora V3.2 weights; LightX2V's 4-step LoRAs)
